agent.problem: Stop 2, card 9 quotes "I will ___ your days.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

agent.problem: Solomon is introduced only with "Meet Solomon." The opening never says simply who he is, such as Israel's king.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

agent.problem: Card 13 has already said that Solomon does not know how to go out or come in. That directly gives away the answer to card 14, which asks whether Solomon says he already knows how to lead.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

agent.problem: Cards 3, 5, 11 and 13 provide no preceding setup from which their answers can be reasoned: the third thing Solomon did not request, God's uniqueness promise, Solomon's return to Jerusalem and his closing feast. Four of the stop's seven choice cards are therefore discovery questions, so informed guesses do not make up most of the stop.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

human.problem: The wrong answers 'The city of Gezer' and 'The city of Megiddo' are false in 1 Kings 3:1-15. But Solomon does build both later (1 Kings 9:15-17), and Gezer is the dowry Pharaoh gives his daughter, Solomon's wife (1 Kings 9:16). A baker who knows this could argue those answers are right. Stop 2, card 7 has the same issue: 'Peace and rest' is something God gives Solomon in 1 Kings 5:4.
human.question: The rules require wrong answers to be false anywhere in the passage, and they encourage real details from elsewhere in the Bible. Should a wrong answer also be ruled out when it is true of the same person somewhere else in Scripture?
